Planning routines, not medical, psychological or financial advice. Add routines here; the pin refill plans only routines no pin has used yet (never two pins alike).

pages.h1: ADHD morning routine: 8 short versions for hard mornings
pages.title: ADHD morning routine: 8 short versions | A Player Mode
pages.meta: Eight ADHD morning routines of four to six steps: low motivation, 15 minutes, late starts, no phone, time blindness, working from home and kids.
pages.definition: An ADHD morning routine is a short, fixed order of steps that takes the decisions out of the first hour, so getting up, dressed and started does not depend on motivation or memory.
pages.quick: Keep it to four to six steps, set most of it up the night before, and end on one small start on the day's must-do. Pick the version below that fits the morning you actually have.
faq: How long should an ADHD morning routine be?
Short enough to survive a bad morning: four to six steps and about 15 to 30 minutes. A long routine breaks the first time you oversleep.
Should I check my phone first thing?
Most people do better checking it after they are dressed and have started one task. Feeds and messages are built to keep you there.
Is this medical advice?
No. These are planning routines, not medical, psychological or treatment advice. Talk to a clinician about ADHD care.

routines.title: ADHD Morning Routine for Low Motivation: 6 Steps That Get You Started
routines.headline: ADHD Morning Routine
routines.description: A six-step ADHD morning routine for days when motivation is low: water before your phone, clothes laid out the night before, one song to get dressed, something small to eat, one must-do written down, then five minutes on it. Planning routine, not medical advice.

routines.title: Morning Routine for ADHD Adults in 15 Minutes
routines.headline: Morning Routine in 15 Minutes
steps: Feet on the floor at the alarm
routines.description: A 15-minute morning routine for ADHD adults: up at the alarm, lights on, face and teeth, clothes from the pile you set out last night, a grab-and-go breakfast and a five-minute buffer before you leave. Planning routine, not medical advice.

routines.title: ADHD Morning Routine Checklist for the Front Door
routines.headline: ADHD Morning Checklist
routines.description: Tape this by the door: keys, wallet and phone, a bag packed the night before, the charger in it, the day's first meeting checked, a filled water bottle, and out five minutes early. A morning checklist for ADHD brains. Not medical advice.

routines.title: Morning Routine When You Wake Up Late: What to Skip and What to Keep
routines.headline: Morning Routine, Woke Up Late
routines.description: Woke up late? Skip the catch-up. Dress, teeth and water, read only the day's first task, send one running-late text, eat on the way and start the day at step one. The full late-start routine is on the page.

routines.title: ADHD Morning Routine Without Your Phone: 6 Steps
routines.headline: Morning Routine, No Phone
routines.description: An ADHD morning routine that keeps the phone out of the first hour: it charges outside the bedroom, a paper list waits on the nightstand, music instead of feeds, the phone after you are dressed, messages after the first task and social apps after lunch.

routines.title: Morning Routine for Time Blindness: Clocks, Timers and a Leave Alarm
routines.headline: Time Blindness Morning Routine
steps: A clock you can see in every room
routines.description: A morning routine for time blindness: a visible clock in every room, a timer on the shower, one alarm for shoes on and one for leave now, the same order every day, and the plan counted back from the time you have to leave. Not medical advice.

routines.title: ADHD Morning Routine for Working From Home
routines.headline: Work-From-Home Morning Routine
routines.description: An ADHD-friendly work-from-home morning: dressed for outside, a desk cleared the night before, coffee then one hard task, messages only after 45 minutes, a stand-up break at 10 and lunch away from the desk.

routines.title: Morning Routine With Kids When You Have ADHD
routines.headline: Morning Routine With Kids
steps: Shoes and bags by the door
Two calm minutes in the car
routines.description: A morning routine for ADHD parents: lunches packed the night before, shoes and bags by the door, a picture checklist for each child, your coffee before their breakfast, one leave-time alarm for everyone and two calm minutes in the car.

pages.h1: Weekly planning routine: 8 ways to plan the week in under 30 minutes
pages.title: Weekly planning routine in under 30 minutes | A Player Mode
pages.meta: Eight weekly planning routines of four to six steps: 20-minute planning, a Sunday reset, busy weeks, founders, review questions and no overplanning.
pages.definition: A weekly planning routine is a short, repeated session, usually 15 to 30 minutes, where you clear last week, place the fixed commitments and choose a few outcomes for the week ahead.
pages.quick: Do it at the same time each week, fixed things first, then no more than three outcomes. Leave empty space every day; a full plan breaks on the first surprise.
faq: When is the best time to plan the week?
Whenever you can protect it every week: Sunday evening, Monday morning or Friday afternoon all work. The habit matters more than the day.
How many goals should a week have?
Three outcomes is a good ceiling. More than that and the week turns into a wish list.
Do I need a paper planner?
No. One page, a notes app or a calendar is enough. What matters is that the plan fits on one screen or one sheet.

routines.title: Weekly Planning Routine in 20 Minutes: 6 Steps
routines.headline: Weekly Planning in 20 Minutes
routines.description: Plan your week in 20 minutes: clear last week's list, copy in the fixed appointments, pick three outcomes, give each a day, block one focus slot every day and leave Friday afternoon open for what slips.

routines.title: Sunday Reset Routine for the Week Ahead
routines.headline: Sunday Reset Routine
routines.description: A Sunday reset routine that sets up the week: laundry on and dishes done, a look at the calendar, three easy dinners planned, Monday's bag packed, Monday's first task chosen and bed 30 minutes early.

routines.title: Weekly Planner Method for Busy Weeks
routines.headline: Weekly Planner for Busy Weeks
routines.description: A weekly planner method for busy weeks: list every fixed commitment, mark the two busiest days, move what can wait, keep one priority per day, batch errands into one trip and fit the whole week on one page.

routines.title: Weekly Reset Checklist You Can Finish in 15 Minutes
routines.headline: Weekly Reset Checklist
routines.description: A 15-minute weekly reset checklist: empty your bag and desk, get the inbox under ten, pay or schedule the bills, delete finished tasks, check next week's deadlines and set Monday's first task.

routines.title: Weekly Planning for Founders: A 6-Step Monday Routine
routines.headline: Weekly Planning for Founders
steps: Pick the one number that matters
routines.description: A weekly planning routine for founders: review last week's numbers, pick the one number that matters this week, choose three outcomes, block two deep-work mornings, batch meetings onto two days and book the Friday review.

routines.title: Weekly Planning Review: 6 Questions in 10 Minutes
routines.headline: Weekly Review Questions
steps: When is my first focus block?
routines.description: Six weekly review questions that take ten minutes: what got done, what slipped and why, what you promised people, what you can drop, next week's three outcomes and when your first focus block is.

routines.title: Weekly Planner Routine Without Overplanning
routines.headline: Weekly Planner, No Overplanning
steps: Only a top task each day
routines.description: Plan the week without overplanning: one page instead of a planner spread, three outcomes only, fixed things first, empty space every day, just a top task for each day, and stop after 20 minutes.

routines.title: Weekly Planning on Monday Morning in 15 Minutes
routines.headline: Monday Weekly Planning
routines.description: A Monday morning weekly planning routine that takes 15 minutes: open the calendar before the inbox, note what changed since Friday, pick three outcomes, book them into real slots, tell people what you will deliver and start outcome one.

pages.h1: Time blocking for busy days: 8 schedules that hold up
pages.title: Time blocking for busy days: 8 schedules | A Player Mode
pages.meta: Eight time blocking routines of four to six steps: busy days, meeting-heavy days, kids at home, a 9 to 5, founders, deep work and chaotic days.
pages.definition: Time blocking is planning your day as blocks on the calendar, each with one job, so the most important work has a time and the rest fits around it.
pages.quick: Place fixed things first, give the one hard task the best block, add buffers after meetings, and put the end of the day on the calendar too.
faq: How long should a time block be?
Between 30 and 90 minutes for focused work. Shorter blocks suit admin and replies; longer ones need a break inside them.
What if the day blows up?
Re-plan once, at lunch: keep the must-do, move the rest. A block that slips is information, not failure.
Do I block every minute?
No. Leave buffers. A day with no slack fails at the first late meeting.

routines.title: Time Blocking for Busy Days: 6 Blocks That Hold
routines.headline: Time Blocking for Busy Days
steps: A stop time on the calendar
routines.description: Time blocking for busy days: put fixed meetings in first, protect one 90-minute focus block, give admin 30 minutes, add a buffer after every meeting, make lunch a real block and put your stop time on the calendar.

routines.title: Time Blocking Template for a Meeting-Heavy Day
routines.headline: Time Blocking Template
routines.description: A time blocking template for a day full of meetings: a focus block before 9, meetings back to back after that, a 15-minute catch-up at noon, replies in one 30-minute block, tomorrow's prep at 4 and nothing new after 5.

routines.title: Time Blocking With Kids at Home: A Realistic Schedule
routines.headline: Time Blocking With Kids Home
steps: Work while they nap or sleep
routines.description: Time blocking with kids at home: work while they nap or sleep, use short 45-minute blocks, make their screen time your call time, share a calendar with your partner, batch errands and plan for interruptions.

routines.title: Daily Routine Schedule for a 9 to 5 Job
routines.headline: Daily Routine for a 9 to 5
routines.description: A daily routine schedule for a 9 to 5: up at 6:30, one personal task at 7:30, the hardest work at 9, a walk and lunch at 12:30, admin and replies at 3 and a shutdown list at 5.

routines.title: Time Blocking for Founders: Build, Sell, Lead
routines.headline: Time Blocking for Founders
routines.description: Time blocking for founders: mornings for building, sales calls after 1, team time on Tuesdays, the inbox twice a day, no meetings on Wednesday morning and a weekly review on Friday at 4.

routines.title: Time Blocking When Every Day Is Different
routines.headline: Time Blocking, Changing Days
steps: Fit it in the biggest gap
routines.description: Time blocking when no two days look alike: plan tomorrow the night before, place the fixed things first, pick one must-do, fit it into the biggest gap, keep everything else on a list and re-plan once at lunch.

routines.title: Time Blocking for Deep Work: 6 Rules
routines.headline: Time Blocking for Deep Work
routines.description: Six rules for deep-work time blocks: the phone in another room, one task per block, 90 minutes then a break, the same time each day, your status set to busy and a note of where you stopped.

routines.title: Daily Routine for a Chaotic Day: Keep One Thing Moving
routines.headline: Daily Routine, Chaotic Day
routines.description: A daily routine for chaotic days: write down the three fixed things, pick one thing that must move, do it before noon, batch the small tasks, say no to one request and end with tomorrow's first step.

pages.h1: Minimum day: what to do after a bad day (8 short routines)
pages.title: Minimum day: what to do after a bad day | A Player Mode
pages.meta: Eight minimum-day routines of four to six steps for bad days, low energy, falling off track and restarting habits without a catch-up list.
pages.definition: A minimum day is a deliberately small plan for a bad or low-energy day: basic care, one task that keeps things moving, and no catch-up list, so a missed day does not become a missed week.
pages.quick: Shrink the plan instead of skipping it. Do the smallest version of what matters, drop the catch-up, and go back to the normal plan tomorrow.
faq: Is a minimum day the same as a rest day?
Not quite. A rest day does nothing on purpose; a minimum day keeps one or two things moving so restarting tomorrow is easy.
What if I miss two days?
Never miss twice is a guide, not a rule to punish yourself with. Start again with the smallest version today.
Is this mental health advice?
No. These are planning routines. If bad days are frequent or heavy, talk to someone qualified.

routines.title: Productivity on a Bad Day: The Minimum Day in 6 Steps
routines.headline: Bad Day Routine
steps: One task that keeps things moving
routines.description: A bad day routine called the minimum day: water and food, one task that keeps things moving, one reply you owe, ten minutes outside, no catch-up list, and bed on time. Tomorrow you go back to the normal plan.

routines.title: Habit Tracker Rule: Never Miss Twice
routines.headline: Habit Tracker Rule
routines.description: The never miss twice habit tracker rule: missing yesterday is fine, do the tiny version today, two minutes counts, tick it done, never try to make up missed days and go back to normal tomorrow.

routines.title: Productivity on a Low-Energy Day: 6 Steps
routines.headline: Low-Energy Day Productivity
routines.description: Productivity for a low-energy day: pick one must-do, make it smaller, do it first, cancel one optional thing, leave easy tasks for after lunch and stop once the must-do is done.

routines.title: Productivity Reset After a Bad Day: 10 Minutes
routines.headline: Bad Day Reset
routines.description: A ten-minute bad day reset: stand up and drink water, write down what is bothering you, circle the parts you control, pick one small next step, do it now and tell one person how the day is going.

routines.title: Goal Setting After Falling Off Track
routines.headline: Goal Setting, Off Track
steps: Keep the goal, shrink the step
routines.description: Goal setting after you fall off track: do not restart from zero, keep the goal and shrink the step, set a seven-day minimum, track only yes or no, review on day eight and only then add one step.

routines.title: Productivity Checklist for a Minimum Viable Day
routines.headline: Minimum Viable Day Checklist
routines.description: A minimum viable day checklist: food, water and sleep, one work task, one home task, one kind word to someone, no new commitments, and when those are done the day is done.

routines.title: Productivity on a Tired Day: What to Move and What to Keep
routines.headline: Tired Day Productivity
routines.description: Productivity on a tired day: the hardest thing before noon, move one meeting, short tasks after lunch, a ten-minute walk outside, no big decisions today and an early night.

routines.title: Habit Tracker for Restarting: 2 Habits, Not 10
routines.headline: Habit Tracker for Restarting
steps: Tick a box, no streak score
routines.description: A habit tracker for restarting: choose two habits instead of ten, use the smallest version of each, do them at the same time every day, tick a box without a streak score, never miss twice and review on Sundays.

pages.h1: Family weekly reset: 8 routines that lighten the mental load
pages.title: Family weekly reset: 8 routines | A Player Mode
pages.meta: Eight family routines of four to six steps: a Sunday reset, weekly planning for parents, mornings, evenings, the mental load and monthly family admin.
pages.definition: A family weekly reset is a short, shared check-in, often on Sunday, where the household looks at the week, splits who does what and sets up the busiest days before they arrive.
pages.quick: Keep it under 30 minutes, use one shared calendar, decide who owns each job from start to finish, and plan one fun thing so the reset is not only chores.
faq: How long should a family reset take?
Fifteen to thirty minutes. If it runs longer, the list is too big for one week.
What is the mental load?
The invisible work of remembering, planning and checking everything a household needs. Writing it down and splitting it is the first step.
Do kids need to join?
Older kids can own one job each. Younger kids only need the picture checklist that comes out of it.

routines.title: Family Routine: Sunday Reset in 30 Minutes
routines.headline: Family Sunday Reset
routines.description: A 30-minute family Sunday reset: look at the week together, write who is where on which day, plan three easy dinners, get bags and uniforms ready, pick one fun thing and set Monday's wake-up time.

routines.title: Family Weekly Planning for Busy Parents
routines.headline: Family Weekly Planning
steps: A backup plan for sick days
routines.description: Weekly planning for busy parents: one shared calendar, a 15-minute Sunday check-in, pickups split by day, meals on a whiteboard, a backup plan for sick days and date night on the calendar.

routines.title: Family Morning Routine Checklist for School Days
routines.headline: Family Morning Routine
steps: A picture list for each kid
Shoes and bags by the door
routines.description: A family morning routine for school days: clothes out the night before, the same breakfast every school day, a picture list for each child, shoes and bags by the door, one leave-time alarm and a five-minute buffer.

routines.title: Family Evening Routine That Sets Up Tomorrow
routines.headline: Family Evening Routine
steps: Screens off an hour before bed
routines.description: A family evening routine that sets up the next day: dinner at a set time, bags packed, screens off an hour before bed, bath, book, bed, parents check tomorrow, and a ten-minute tidy together.

routines.title: Balanced Life Weekly Check: 6 Questions
routines.headline: Balanced Life Weekly Check
routines.description: A balanced life weekly check in six questions: was focus time protected, did you move three times, did everyone get one-on-one time, was one home admin job done, was there one slow evening, and what is the one change for next week.

routines.title: Gratitude Routine for Families That Takes 2 Minutes
routines.headline: Family Gratitude Routine
steps: A gratitude jar on the counter
routines.description: A family gratitude routine that takes two minutes: ask for the best part of the day at dinner, write one thank-you note a week, keep a gratitude jar on the counter, name one thing at bedtime, listen without fixing and keep it short.

routines.title: Family Routine for Sharing the Mental Load
routines.headline: Family Mental Load Routine
steps: Each owns tasks start to end
routines.description: A family routine for sharing the mental load: write every open loop down, split the list in two, each person owns tasks from start to finish, the calendar holds the reminders, sync for ten minutes on Sunday and swap one job a month.

routines.title: Family Admin Routine: 30 Minutes a Month
routines.headline: Family Admin Routine
routines.description: A monthly family admin routine: check bills and renewals, list upcoming birthdays, book appointments, collect school forms and dates, cancel unused subscriptions, all in 30 minutes on the first Sunday of the month.

pages.h1: Founder daily routine: 8 productivity routines that protect the work
pages.title: Founder daily routine: 8 productivity routines | A Player Mode
pages.meta: Eight founder routines of four to six steps: a daily productivity routine, 90-day goals, mornings, a weekly scorecard, shutdown and follow-ups.
pages.definition: A founder daily routine is a fixed shape for the working day that protects the time spent building and selling from the inbox, meetings and the constant pull of small requests.
pages.quick: Decide the day's one outcome before opening the inbox, build first, batch calls and replies, and close the day by choosing tomorrow's first task.
faq: How many hours should a founder block for deep work?
Two to four focused hours a day is a realistic ceiling for most people; protect at least one 90-minute block.
Should founders check email first thing?
Usually not. Decide the day's outcome and start it first; the inbox can wait an hour or two.
Are these results guaranteed?
No. They are example routines; results vary with the business and the person.

routines.title: Productivity Routine for Founders: The Daily Six
routines.headline: Founder Productivity Routine
routines.description: A daily productivity routine for founders: write today's one outcome, build before opening email, check the inbox at 11 and 4, put calls in one afternoon block, ship something small and close with tomorrow's top task.

routines.title: Goal Setting for Founders: A 90-Day Plan in 6 Steps
routines.headline: 90-Day Goal Setting
steps: Kill a bet that isn't working
routines.description: Ninety-day goal setting for founders: one goal with one number, three bets to move it, a weekly check on Friday at 4, kill a bet that is not working, keep a wins list and review at day 45.

routines.title: Productivity Morning Routine for Founders
routines.headline: Founder Morning Routine
routines.description: A founder morning routine: up, water and no inbox, 20 minutes of planning, 90 minutes on the hardest thing, then the team check-in, messages after 11 and lunch away from the laptop.

routines.title: Productivity System for a Solo Founder
routines.headline: Solo Founder System
routines.description: A simple productivity system for a solo founder: one list for everything, one calendar, a daily top three, a weekly review, a monthly numbers check and a quarterly goal reset.

routines.title: Goal Setting: A Weekly Founder Scorecard
routines.headline: Weekly Founder Scorecard
routines.description: A weekly founder scorecard for goal setting: this week's key number, one thing shipped, conversations with customers, the biggest blocker, what you will stop doing and next week's one outcome.

routines.title: Productivity: An End-of-Day Shutdown Routine
routines.headline: End-of-Day Shutdown
routines.description: A ten-minute end-of-day shutdown routine: write what got done, move unfinished tasks, pick tomorrow's first task, clear the desk, close every tab and say done for today.

routines.title: Productivity: A Follow-Up Routine for Busy Founders
routines.headline: Founder Follow-Up Routine
steps: List who you owe a reply
routines.description: A follow-up routine for busy founders: list who you owe a reply, answer three before noon, put every promise on the calendar, keep answers to two lines, clear the rest on Friday so nothing waits on memory.

routines.title: Habit Tracker for Founders: 6 Daily Yes-or-No Boxes
routines.headline: Founder Habit Tracker
routines.description: A founder habit tracker with six yes-or-no boxes: deep work block done, talked to a customer, moved for 20 minutes, inbox under control, home by dinner. Tick yes or no, nothing else.
